report.source_text: The patient was isolated and a blood sample was taken and sent to the national laboratory of viral hemorrhagic fever on 22 January 2018. He was given ribavirin 30 mg/kg IV (maximum, 2 g) loading dose to be followed by 15 mg/kg IV (maximum, 1 g) every 6 h for 4 days, vitamin K1, transfusion of two isogroup isorhesius blood bags, and oxygen therapy.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old man presented with a week of bloody and febrile diarrhea, followed by bilious vomiting, odynophagia, intense headaches, and generalized aches. Initial physical examination on admission (Jan 18, 2018) revealed a temperature of 39 °C, tachycardia, polypnea, and elevated blood pressure. Initial laboratory tests showed mild thrombocytopenia (platelets 123 109/L) and elevated liver enzymes (ALT 82 IU/L, AST 62 IU/L), with negative malaria thick drop and HIV status. On hospitalization day 3, persistent fever, melena, facial puffiness, and conjunctival hemorrhage led to suspicion of viral hemorrhagic fever. On day 4 (Jan 22, 2018), the patient was isolated, a blood sample was sent for viral hemorrhagic fever testing, and treatment with ribavirin, vitamin K1, blood transfusion, and oxygen therapy was initiated. The patient died on day 6 (Jan 23, 2018) after repeated convulsions with bradypnea and cardio-circulatory arrest. Lassa hemorrhagic fever was confirmed by Reverse Transcriptase Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) assay on January 24, 2018, from the sample taken on Jan 22, noted as 'post-mortem day 1'.
